plans.note: Primary review at Section 21; check mutuality of the cap, the multiplier of Fees, exclusion of indirect damages, and the scope of "Excluded Claims" as defined in Section 1. Confirm data breach, confidentiality and IP indemnity sit outside the cap.

Section 20 should contain Vendor IP infringement plus negligence/wilful misconduct and data breach indemnities; verify any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data rights only) and that Section 21 does not cap Excluded Claims. Cross-check Sections 14 and 15 for IP/data hooks.

No dedicated restrictive covenant section in the outline; scan Sections 2 (scope), 12 (Customer responsibilities), 13 (access/licence restrictions) and 30 (General) for disguised limits on competing products or in-house builds before concluding absent.

Look for sole-source or "all requirements" language in Sections 2 and 4 (Order Forms and Affiliate Orders) and in Sections 12 and 7; any exclusivity should be deleted or narrowed to the specific ordered scope.

Direction check: an MFN favouring us is acceptable, but any obligation for us to offer Vendor best terms must go. Most likely to appear in pricing (Section 7) or ordering (Section 4); otherwise absent.

No standalone non-solicit heading; check Section 30 (General) and Sections 12 and 16 for hiring restrictions. If present, seek mutuality, 12-month cap and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 is the main termination clause; confirm Customer convenience termination on ~30 days' notice without penalty or early-termination fee (check Sections 7 and 10 for wind-down charges) and that Vendor has no mid-term convenience right.
Section 8 governs term and renewal; test the non-renewal notice window (target 30 days, not 90) and any uplift cap on renewal Fees, cross-checking the pricing mechanics in Section 7.

Section 28 sets governing law, venue and any arbitration; confirm an approved jurisdiction (NY, DE, CA or England and Wales) and courts rather than offshore arbitration. Check Section 29 only if venue/service of process is cross-referenced.

Section 24 covers assignment and change of control; secure our right to assign to Affiliates and successors without consent and delete any Vendor termination or repricing right triggered by our change of control. Section 30 may hold a residual assignment clause.

Direction check in Section 14 (Deliverables ownership) and Section 15 (Customer Data): we must own paid-for Deliverables and all Customer Data, with no assignment or broad licence-back to Vendor. Review the Section 1 definitions of Deliverable, Customer Data and Vendor Technology, and any feedback/licence language in Section 13.

Section 13 is the licence grant; extend scope to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and remove any "revocable at will" or unilateral suspension language. Cross-check Affiliate ordering in Section 4.

Section 22 likely contains Vendor audits of our usage: limit to once per 12 months, 10+ business days' notice, business hours, remote/off-site where feasible, at Vendor's cost absent material underpayment. Section 23 records obligations may support or duplicate this.
Direction check: service credits in Section 3 favour us and stay, but strike liquidated damages, penalties or interest-style charges payable by us in Sections 7, 9 and 21.

Section 19 is the warranty clause; seek a professional-services and Deliverable conformity warranty of at least 90 days with re-performance plus refund as remedy, and resist "sole remedy" narrowing. Cross-check performance standards in Section 3 and acceptance in Section 6.

Section 18 exists; confirm coverage lines and limits (CGL, professional/E&O, cyber, workers' comp), certificate and notice-of-cancellation obligations, given Vendor handles Customer Data under Sections 15 and 17.

Check Sections 7 and 4 for committed spend, minimum volumes or take-or-pay true-ups and any non-reduction of quantities at renewal in Section 8; if present, pair with a convenience exit or reduction right.

Section 11 addresses transition assistance and data return; verify a minimum assistance period at then-current rates, export in a usable format, and deletion/certification, reconciled with the post-termination effects in Section 10 and data rights in Section 15.
